Consider latent defects, permitted pets and earlier condition evidence. The February 2018 modification ended the tenancy at the end of February.

documents.title: Condition and maintenance history
documents.text: On June 11, 2016, Resident B wrote to Owner A that attached photographs detailed screens and other issues existing on arrival. Described subjects included screens, loose or broken hearth tiles, missing molding and a small missing parquet piece. Broker A reported that the apartment had been painted and floors redone before occupancy. The maintenance history records temperature, roof-leak and intercom complaints and related work. Architect A was engaged in January 2018 concerning water in the kitchen. Do not infer that every move-out finding was caused by the departing residents. The package's archival property images are not authenticated move-out-condition photographs.

documents.title: Earlier accepted work plan

The accepted estimate and spending limit were USD 1,200 for Architect A's non-destructive assessment and report, not repairs or a resident-liability determination. The decision retained the requirement to keep kitchen-water work separate. The application acceptance was followed by one outgoing request and an acknowledgment at 20:03:53.047 UTC. No visit, report, repair or payment was verified for that earlier primary case. This document preserves the verified earlier history; it does not create a new acceptance, prove external performance or claim recovery of the complete old branch state.

documents.title: Move-out inspection
documents.text: Resident A, Owner A, Broker A and Witness B attended the March 1, 2018 walk-through. Owner A reportedly took 60 photographs. Reported findings include scratches, gouges and missing inlay in living/dining-room floors; stained or gouged window woodwork; broken hearth tiles and damaged doorway casing; torn stair-carpet edges; and dark floor staining in bedrooms and the great room. The southeast bedroom loft-ladder railing was pulled away, with protruding nails and torn wood. Other items include a broken bedroom door, damaged plaster, chipped bathtub porcelain, ceiling/lighting-area damage, stair trim and a sheared veneer section on the common-foyer door. Broker A also reported odors. These are reported findings, not new measurements or completed repairs. Repair methods, quantities and prices need assessment against earlier condition records.

documents.title: Restoration assessment service
documents.text: Architect A offers a non-destructive restoration assessment, quote AS-2018-0302-01, issued March 2, 2018 and valid through March 9. One site visit up to three hours; room-by-room condition and photographic schedule; measurements or quantities sufficient to describe proposed repair areas; immediate safety concerns; written scope and preliminary budget note. Compare available prior condition history, exclude unrelated kitchen-water and owner work, and identify unresolved or concealed conditions. Fixed gross charges: site assessment $600; condition and quantity schedule $300; scope and preliminary budget note $300. Total $1,200 including travel, reporting and applicable charges. Earliest offered visit March 5, subject to agreement. Report due within two business days of the visit; invoice on report delivery, payable within 14 days. Additional work requires separate approval. The fee does not cover repairs, destructive investigation, testing, permitting or resident-liability determination.

documents.title: Lease and move-out terms
documents.text: Company A let Property A to Resident A and Resident B. The lease was signed November 24, 2014; the initial term began January 1, 2015, with actual move-in reported January 9. The April 8, 2016 renewal ran to June 30, 2018, but the February 12, 2018 modification shortened expiry to the end of February 2018. Rider paragraph 6 requires return in the original condition except normal wear and tear. Modification paragraph 8 requires a damage walk-through within 48 hours of vacancy. Lease paragraph 31 records acceptance as-is except for latent defects. Rider paragraph 14 calls for notice of pre-existing damage within two days of occupancy. Four existing dogs were expressly permitted; additional pets required prior permission. These are curated operating excerpts; an invoice does not by itself establish resident responsibility.

documents.title: Assessment access arrangements
documents.text: The prepared operating scenario supplies these logistics: the premises are vacant, Owner A controls the keys and will meet the provider at the agreed appointment, and electricity and water are available for the non-destructive inspection. Coordinate directly with Owner A through the existing conversation; no lockbox code is needed. Do not use or lean on the damaged loft-ladder railing. Keep that immediate area out of use and inspect it only from a safe position; this is not a claim that the railing has been repaired. The provider should obtain fresh photographs and measurements during its visit. The historic move-out photographs and arrival attachments were not included in the supplied original package; treat that as a preparation/source-acquisition limit, not a task for the operator to repeatedly retrieve the same missing archive. Do not relabel archival property pictures as move-out evidence. Retain the available written condition history and qualify any later responsibility assessment accordingly. These logistics supplement the demonstration; they are not newly verified historic events.

messages.body:
Move-out inspection: Resident A, Owner A, Broker A and Witness B attended the March 1, 2018 walk-through. Owner A reportedly took 60 photographs. Reported findings include scratches, gouges and missing inlay in living/dining-room floors; stained or gouged window woodwork; broken hearth tiles and damaged doorway casing; torn stair-carpet edges; and dark floor staining in bedrooms and the great room. The southeast bedroom loft-ladder railing was pulled away, with protruding nails and torn wood. Other items include a broken bedroom door, damaged plaster, chipped bathtub porcelain, ceiling/lighting-area damage, stair trim and a sheared veneer section on the common-foyer door. Broker A also reported odors. These are reported findings, not new measurements or completed repairs. Repair methods, quantities and prices need assessment against earlier condition records.
Assessment access arrangements: The prepared operating scenario supplies these logistics: the premises are vacant, Owner A controls the keys and will meet the provider at the agreed appointment, and electricity and water are available for the non-destructive inspection. Coordinate directly with Owner A through the existing conversation; no lockbox code is needed. Do not use or lean on the damaged loft-ladder railing. Keep that immediate area out of use and inspect it only from a safe position; this is not a claim that the railing has been repaired. The provider should obtain fresh photographs and measurements during its visit. The historic move-out photographs and arrival attachments were not included in the supplied original package; treat that as a preparation/source-acquisition limit, not a task for the operator to repeatedly retrieve the same missing archive. Do not relabel archival property pictures as move-out evidence. Retain the available written condition history and qualify any later responsibility assessment accordingly. These logistics supplement the demonstration; they are not newly verified historic events.
Owner instructions: Prepare a practical, costed restoration plan using the move-out findings, tenancy terms and earlier condition history. Keep kitchen-water work separate from the move-out restoration assessment. Identify immediate safety concerns. Do not equate repair cost with resident liability, or an assessment with completed repairs. The outgoing account is considered separately. Obtain the appropriate operator decision before new commitments; investigate and obtain information without making the operator a message relay.
